newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: W&H has no explanation for rise in shares.
newsitem.headline: W&H has no explanation for rise in shares.

text.p: New Zealand publisher Wilson and Horton said it had no information to explain a sharp rise in its shares on Wednesday.
The stock closed 55 cents higher at NZ$11.80.
"This company is not in possession of any information which if made available to the public might reasonably be regarded as an explanation for the price variation," W&H said.

"The company does not have any reason to believe or suspect that any person has bought or sold securities on the basis of such information. The company is not about to make any announcements to the exchange."
Rumours circulated the share market that Tony O'Reilly's Independent Newspapers was seeking the remaining 15 percent of Wilson and Horton.
Total turnover in the stock was worth NZ$838,308, the biggest parcel being 25,000 shares sold at the closing price.
Brokers were treating the talk with scepticism, but they noted W&H attracted reasonable turnover last week.
They also noted that, with both Wilson and Horton and INP having recently released their financial results, such a move might be timely from a disclosure perspective.
INP spokesman Paul Hemsley said there was no notice pending, but added it was no secret INP would like further increase its 85 percent holding following its NZ$11 per share bid late last year.
